newsitem.title: UK: Clydeport chairman says he retires.
newsitem.headline: Clydeport chairman says he retires.

text.p: Clydeport Plc chairman John Mather today said he would retire and be succeeded by James Millar as acting chairman. Millar is currently deputy chairman.
Mather, 60, told the company's annual general meeting he had suffered from ill health in recent months.
"I accordingly will step down as chairman of the company and retire from the board with effect from the conclusion of today's meeting," he said.

"I am delighted to announce that James Millar, currently deputy chairman, will succeed me as acting chairman. James has been a non-executive director of Clydeport since flotation and during that time has made a substantial contribution to the affairs of the company," he added.

Clydeport's former managing director David Hunt left the company in February 1997 to pursue personal interests, Mather added. " The board are well down the road in the selection of David's successor and an announcement should be made shortly."
Mather also said: "The present year has started well, with results to date ahead of our expectations."
Hunterston has discharged more than 300,000 tonnes of coal for ScottishPower, Mather said, and broadened its customer base from one power generator to three.
He said Glasgow's scrap traffic is performing well and there are signs of the beginning of a recovery in the animal feed market.
But he added: "Volumes of steel handled through King George V Dock fell below expectations, a position likely to continue for the foreseeable future."

"The main challenge at the Port of Greenock remains the replacement of the Tate and Lyle sugar traffic which will come to an end in the autumn of this year. We continue actively to pursue replacement traffics."
